item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Damn it Roget, you've put me between a rock and a hard place.

Fundamentally, I love this GOI document. I love that someone is finally trying to give Alexylva one, I love the idea you went for what it is.

But I do not think the actual content fits. The image I got of Alexylva from the skips I've read was of a colossal, Neo-Ancient Greek school.1 This reads more along the lines of a Oneiroi district based upon Greece - it repeatedly claims to be focused on knowledge and learning, but then incessantly cites these weird and blatantly nonsensical rituals throughout it that, again, feel vastly more fitting in a Oneiroi setting.2

Again, I love the presentation and idea of this Alexylva GOI document, but the actual content fits far, far better with the Oneiroi than Alexylva.

Footnotes
1. I know 'Neo-Ancient' doesn't make sense. I mean something along the lines of 'Ancient Greece, but cyberpunk-ish'. Modern/Advanced/Futuristic technology in the setting of Ancient Greece.
2. 'DOUSE THEM IN THE CLEANSING LIQUID OF THOUGHT,' 'DISCOVER HOW TO PLUMB THE MIND IN OTHERS TO FACILITATE LIFE ADVANTAGE,' 'JUDGEMENT WILL BE MADE ON CRYING OUT TO THE INFINITE UNKNOWN AND WILLINGNESS TO PROSELYTIZE THE SELF BEFORE THE YAWNING VOID,' etc.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Well, I was trying to tell a story in the background by the progression of the news stories and articles, and I wasn't attempting to portray their technology level as jokey or primitive. I wasn't trying to make something not intended to be taken seriously.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I dislike this on a fundamental level. I don't think it's poorly written, but it's such a straight port of Universe Prime sensibilities over to Alexvya that it really feels like it ceases to be about them and what makes them entertaining and transitions into a Flintstones-esque parody of Uni tropes. I can totally see other people enjoying it as a matter of interdimensional magitech hijinks, but it's definitely not for me.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Well, the writing style is me trying to capture a culture with different language traditions that's also writing propaganda. I didn't throw the job titles or nomenclature randomly, I tried to give it an internal logic. I didn't use any translation software in writing this. I've also done my best to make it work on phones, I've got it working on mine.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm rather meh on this. Outside of the piece itself, writing something with elements you know most readers won't have installed/activated and then asking/expecting them to do so is a terrible idea.

For the piece… meh? The broken English thing is blown way out of proportion compared to the Alexylva SCP translations I can remember. The tone in those was archaic, this reads like you ran it back and forth trough translation software a few times. There was no pattern to it either; just, sometimes it follows normal sentence structure, sometimes it doesn't.

All the random mystical details and the extent to which they combined with modern stuff felt random entirely for randomness's sake, as did the vastly different styles between the images. I definitely got some minor Night Vale vibes there, but in Night Vale that's the whole point. There were a few parts that I quite enjoyed, but not enough to make up for how un-interestingly inconsistent this was.

(Edit: For a clear example, the titles of the people involved in the paper don't read like you were trying to re-interpret ancient positions. They read like you threw them together at random.)

-1

Some instructions on activating special characters if you can't read the numbers is here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Special_characters

They're phonecian numerals so you don't necessarily need to know them to read and understand the article.
